Piezoelectric strain \(d_{ij}\) is large only in non-centrosymmetric crystals that combine (i) a soft lattice and (ii) highly polarizable, preferably ns² lone-pair, cations. All 100 pool entries are non-centrosymmetric, so ranking is about chemistry + structure type. Direct isostructural matches in the training set dominate.

**1. c043 K₃SbS₄ (I-43m)**  
Identical 8-atom I-43m tetrahedral network as Na₃SbS₄ (\(d=149\)) and TaTl₃S₄ (\(d=132\)). Substituting Na⁺ by larger K⁺ increases the volume per atom (23 → 28 Å³) and should soften the lattice further. This is the cleanest high-\(d\) analog in the pool.

**2. c025 InGeCl₃ (R3m, 5-atom cell)**  
ABX₃ perovskite with a small rhombohedral distortion (cell angles ~87–93°, vs 90° cubic) — the same 5-atom polar perovskite motif as RbPbBr₃ (\(d=154\), Pm). Oxidation states In⁺ (5s²) + Ge²⁺ (4s²) put **two** lone pairs on the lattice. Training perovskites without a B-site lone pair are essentially zero (RbCaCl₃, SrHfO₃), while lone-pair ones are huge (RbPbBr₃ 154, TiPbO₃ 79). Being only ~3° from cubic implies a soft polar mode and large \(d\).

**3. c041 KGeCl₃ (R3c)**  
The chemically closer analog of RbPbBr₃: alkali + Ge²⁺ 4s² + halide, in the classic R3c ferroelectric perovskite family (CsGeCl₃-type). Rhombohedral angle 63.3° vs 60° cubic, i.e. a similarly small distortion. Cl is stiffer than Br and Ge less polarizable than Pb, so \(d\) should be below 154 but still well into the upper tail.

**4. c037 Tl₃SbS₃ (R3m, 7 atoms)**  
Isostructural to Tl₃AsS₃ (\(d=36\)) and Tl₃AsSe₃ (\(d=37\)). Replacing As by more polarizable Sb, with the same Tl 6s² network, points to \(\sim 35{-}45\) pC/N with very high confidence.

**5. c036 SiS₂ (I-42d, 6-atom MX₂)**  
Same zincblende-derived I-42d MX₂ framework as GeS₂ (\(d=38\)), GeSe₂ (\(d=39\)) and TiS₂ (\(d=104\)). A group-14 disulfide should track GeS₂ more than TiS₂, but the structure type itself is clearly piezo-active and the TiS₂ match gives additional upside.

Other pool crystals that are merely “good not great”: chalcopyrites (ZnGeP₂ ~ CdGeP₂ \(=19\) / CdSnP₂ \(=44\)), I-4 defect chalcopyrites (Al₂HgSe₄, Na₂CdSnS₄ ~ 17–27), Ag sulfides (YAgS₂), and zincblende CuI/CdSe/ZnS (typical \(d\sim 10{-}30\)). Polar hydrides/oxides/nitrides are stiff and sit at the bottom of the training distribution.

Final: c043, c025, c041, c037, c036

              'mendeleev_no', 'row', 'group', 'molar_volume']

def safe_prop(el, prop):

    except:

            feats[f'{prop}_max'] = 0
